account:
Today is day 1, shortly after two in the afternoon. The unusual thing I have heard is repeated, vague talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 11 and Townsfolk 02 said it, and the neighbour has heard similar talk. Neither the neighbour nor the secretary has supplied an eyewitness account or a specific description. I have not seen a change myself. I suspect there may be news circulating that I have not yet understood, but I cannot establish whether anything actually happened, who arranged it, or what it is for. Repetition is not independent confirmation.

The baker is someone I should ask directly. I did not find him in the visible bakery interior this morning, but later saw him at the market stall, and the secretary also reported seeing him there. His absence from the bakery does not itself establish anything unusual. At the mill stall I observed two stacks of sixty-four hay bales; that observation alone tells me nothing about a secret plan or a shortage.

The known bridge business is a municipal visual inspection. The builder delivered a report describing a passable crossing and visible lanterns, with explicit limits: no foundation examination or structural certification. The agreed two emeralds were paid at 07:58, according to the secretary. No repairs or purchases were authorized. I have no evidence connecting that inspection to the bakery rumour.

I am now reviewing office records during my council-letters appointment. The five books I borrowed contain the appointment schedule, bridge records and an older innkeeper request for advance warning of visitors needing food or lodging. I know of no such gathering. I have asked the secretary whether there are new council letters or outstanding decisions, but have not yet heard an answer. Tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage is at three, followed by office time at half past four. That meeting may offer an opportunity to ask carefully about what the neighbour has actually witnessed, without treating hearsay as fact.
